_comment: Known PHP-vs-Python divergences that are ACCEPTED for now. Every entry must name the tracking id of the finding that fixes it; the harness fails when an entry no longer reproduces (so it has to be removed once the fix lands). Anything not listed here that is looser than the original fails the suite.
_note: The list is EMPTY: there is currently no accepted PHP-vs-Python divergence. The five sandbox divergences (sandbox_builtin_alias / sandbox_fstring_eval / sandbox_fstring_os_system / sandbox_fstring_raw / sandbox_hex_getattr) were FIXED in the B5 batch and removed. The `subagent_escalation` entry was removed as well — it was a BAD FIXTURE, not a divergence: the Python side built `PermissionSet(allowed=[...])` with a LIST in a field declared `frozenset[str]`, so `narrow()` raised an AttributeError that the runner's `except Exception` swallowed into a False. With a proper frozenset the original grants the escalation and the port refuses it, i.e. the port is STRICTER — and the scenario now exercises that child-registration path for real.
